title: Reconcile the task-record collision backlog and malformed records
description:
## Summary
`Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` currently fails with 44 issues. The board holds 14 duplicated `TSK-` keys (15 records: TSK-0200 is tripled) plus 30 records missing required schema fields, and `tsk-0206` cannot be deserialized. Because the MemorySmith index is keyed by task key, colliding records silently shadow one another and drop out of `memorysmith_task_list`, so live work is invisible to agents.

## Scope
- Duplicate keys: TSK-0153, 0188, 0189, 0195, 0196, 0197, 0198, 0199, 0200 (x3), 0201, 0202, 0203, 0204, 0205.
- Schema-incomplete records: missing `createdAtUtc`/`updatedAtUtc`/`revision`, plus `tsk-0172` missing `type`.
- Unloadable record: `tsk-0206-align-unity-bone-weight-contract-with-binding-builder.json` (`externalLinks[0]` shape).
- Out of scope: collision-safe *creation* (TSK-0213); normalizer tooling hardening (TSK-0189, Done).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` exits 0 with zero issues.
- `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` reports zero collisions and zero skipped files.
- Each colliding family resolves to exactly one canonical record per mechanism; renumbered or superseded records name their replacement in a note; no mechanism loses its evidence.
- `memorysmith_task_list` returns each distinct mechanism exactly once.
- TSK-0206 either loads correctly or is archived with a named replacement.
- New keys are allocated above the current maximum and do not re-collide.

## Validation
- `pwsh Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` -> 0 issues.
- `pwsh Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` -> "Skipped: 0" and no collision abort.
- `memorysmith_task_list` key set cross-checked against `Data/Tasks/*.json`.

## Findings
- Evidence: `Test-TaskRecords.ps1` run 2026-09-12 -> "FAIL: Task record validation found 44 issue(s)."
- TSK-0200 carries three distinct mechanisms (animated bounds, sparse candidate-region sampling, sparse root-envelope sampling).
- TSK-0189 collides between an `Archived` pose-buffer record and the `Done` normalizer-hardening task.
- This is the fourth recorded recurrence of the task-key collision pattern (2026-09-08, 2026-09-09, TSK-0213, this pass).

## Blockers
- The MemorySmith MCP may not expose key renumbering. If it does not, the reconciliation must extend the sanctioned `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` path. Hand-editing `Data/Tasks/*.json` is prohibited.

## Next Step
Test whether `memorysmith_task_update` can change a task key. If not, add a sanctioned renumber path to the normalizer, reconcile one colliding family as proof, then sweep the remainder.

comments.body:
New evidence (2026-09-12, during TSK-0227 skill work)

`Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` aborts in preflight and writes nothing:

```
FAIL: Normalization preflight found 14 task-identity collision(s). No files were modified.
```

Colliding keys: TSK-0153, TSK-0188, TSK-0189, TSK-0195, TSK-0196, TSK-0197, TSK-0198, TSK-0199, TSK-0200 (3 files), TSK-0201, TSK-0202, TSK-0203, TSK-0204, TSK-0205.

This supersedes the earlier "3 collisions" figure recorded in `/memories/repo/tsk-0197-agent-skill-recommendations-applied.md`; the backlog has grown. The newly created TSK-0227 is not among the collisions, so its key is unique.

Consequence: task-board integrity cannot be claimed until the normalizer passes. This is not caused by the skill work, and the skill change touched no task JSON.

Note: TSK-0197 itself is one of the colliding keys, so any follow-up on the agent/skill guidance record must be reconciled against `tsk-0197-use-cross-thread-safe-allocator-for-background-generation-scratch.json` first.

comments.body:
Reconciled 2026-09-12. Task-record and tooling changes only; no runtime/editor code touched, so no Unity validation was required.

Tooling
- Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1 now accepts -RenumberMap <file>. The whole map is validated before any file is touched (source exists, tsk-####-slug target, key above the current ceiling, target uniqueness) and the pass is idempotent on re-run.
- It also backfills the required schema fields type, createdAtUtc, updatedAtUtc, and revision; a missing timestamp derives from the file's git addition date with a file-system fallback.
- Map: Scripts/task-key-reconciliation-2026-09-12.json (15 entries).

Disposition (old key -> new key, surviving canonical in parentheses)
- TSK-0153 -> TSK-0228 (rest-ground-contact)
- TSK-0188 -> TSK-0229 (make-debug-rig-attachment; 0229 is a superseded duplicate of TSK-0190)
- TSK-0189 -> TSK-0230 (make-task-record-normalization; 0230 is a superseded duplicate of TSK-0191)
- TSK-0195 -> TSK-0231 (sanitize-body-proxy-radius-fallback; duplicate mechanism, 0231 Archived)
- TSK-0196 -> TSK-0232 (short-circuit-nonfinite-limb, Rejected history retained)
- TSK-0197 -> TSK-0233 (use-cross-thread-safe-allocator)
- TSK-0198 -> TSK-0234 (stream-preview-generation-hotpaths)
- TSK-0199 -> TSK-0235 (reuse-resolved-body-frames)
- TSK-0200 -> TSK-0236 and TSK-0200 -> TSK-0237 (sparse-root-envelope-sdf-sampling)
- TSK-0201 -> TSK-0238 (use-root-potential-bounds)
- TSK-0202 -> TSK-0239 (cache-body-arc-length-prefixes; duplicate mechanism)
- TSK-0203 -> TSK-0240 (measure-dense-grid-ownership; duplicate mechanism)
- TSK-0204 -> TSK-0241 (prove-repeatable-determinism)
- TSK-0205 -> TSK-0242 (repair-invalid-implicit-mesh-topology)

Every renumbered record carries a "## Reconciliation" note naming the surviving owner, so no mechanism loses its evidence.

Validation
- pwsh Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1 -> "Fixed: 0  Skipped: 0" (no collision abort).
- pwsh Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1 -> "PASS: Checked 240 task record(s); keys and ids are unique."
- memorysmith_task_get resolves TSK-0195, TSK-0231, and TSK-0239 to distinct records.
- git diff --check clean (only pre-existing ProjectSettings line-ending warnings).

Note: memorysmith_task_update has no id/key parameters, so the MCP cannot renumber; the -RenumberMap pass is the sanctioned path. This is the fifth recorded recurrence of branch-local key allocation (TSK-0136, TSK-0172, TSK-0153, and the TSK-0188/0189 pair, then this pass). Creation-time collision safety remains owned by TSK-0213.
